messages:
maria.santos: Heads-up — acme-prod reported that automatic geo-failover to EU is breaking their compliance audits. They want their traffic pinned to us-west unless they explicitly opt-in to failover.

aj: Got it. How do they identify requests today? header, token claim?

maria.santos: They send X-Tenant-ID: acme-prod and sometimes set X-Region-Pin: true. They asked Support for a console-managed exceptions list to pin tenants or routes.

devon_lee: We already save preferred_region per-tenant in metadata, but our current latency-failover ignores that for SLO reasons. We need a formal exceptions mechanism so we can skip failover for audited tenants.

jen-sre: Proposal: internal Exceptions API + console UI. Minimal API: POST /v1/platform/routing/exceptions {tenant, route_pattern, regions, enforce, expires_at, owner, reason}. Returns exception_id. All writes audited.

aj: UX: console should show a clear banner on the route and tenant pages when an exception exists. Also show a chart "exceptions vs baseline" (dry-run vs enforced) so we can validate before flipping enforcement. Need copy and an owner label.

maria.santos: Quota/capacity note — pinning to a smaller region can blow up reserved capacity there. We should emit a quota_hint metric (tenant, region, expected_rps) so capacity planning and autoscaler get a heads-up.

console-bot: migration plan posted for branch feature/routing-exceptions. Adds routing_exceptions table with schema draft in PR.

devon_lee: Matching precedence thought: exceptions should be evaluated before any latency-based failover or header-driven overrides. Matching order: exact-route + tenant > wildcard-route + tenant > tenant-global > global. Exceptions can be scoped to region-only or zone.

aj: Header precedence question: if request has X-Prefer-Region but an exception exists, what wins? My vote: console exception > tenant preference > header override > global policy. If header is ignored we must log it.

jen-sre: Telemetry: add trace tags routing.exception_id and routing.exception_applied (bool). Also emit metric routing.exception_ignored_header with labels (tenant, header_value) when header was suppressed.

maria.santos: Rollout plan: dry-run (enforce=false) for 48h for acme-prod to collect "would-have" telemetry, then flip to enforce. Support will coordinate communications.

devon_lee: Quick PoC curl for internal API:
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/routing/exceptions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"tenant":"acme-prod","route_pattern":"/v1/generate","regions":["us-west-2"],"scope":"region-only","expires_at":"2025-06-01T00:00:00Z","enforce":false,"reason":"audit pin","owner":"maria.santos"}'
```

aj: Frontend: who picks up modal + banner? @frontend-team. We need admin copy, a toggle for dry-run vs enforce, TTL picker, owner field, and an audit link per exception.

maria.santos: I'll draft copy and post in #product. Include: why pinning exists, dry-run badge, expires_at, audit link, and how to request removal.

jen-sre: Safety net: if pinned region capacity drops below threshold (10% of baseline) alert Ops and optionally allow an emergency fallback after a configurable grace window (default 24h) with full audit. Add a Prom alert PinnedRegionCapacityLow.

devon_lee: I'll add pinned_region_capacity_percent to autoscaler health checks and pipeline the quota_hint metric. Also will include a boolean allow_emergency_fallback on exception policy.

aj: Action items: (1) devon: RFC + schema + precedence, (2) jen: tracing + prometheus alerts + runbook, (3) maria: support comms + console copy, (4) frontend-team: admin modal + banner + chart. Dry-run for acme-prod starts now, reconvene in 48h. :thumbsup:

platform-bot: RFC created: /docs/rfc/routing-exceptions.md by devon_lee

maria.santos: Starting the manual dry-run exception for acme-prod and pinging Support to coordinate.
